critique: The cyan, magenta, violet, and yellow palette, scanlines, grid, and outlined lane geometry form a committed synthwave system. Craft is weakened by excessive simultaneous glow, texture, offset-channel effects, scanlines, particles, grid lines, waveform, and horizon geometry; these stack rather than resolve into a controlled material hierarchy. The PIXEL DANCE title uses multiple misregistered shadows whose edges become muddy, while smaller text is extremely tracked and often too dim. Lane notes use inconsistent hues and border/glow intensities, and the four keycaps do not exactly align with lane centers or share equal spacing. Several elements are visibly cropped at the lower and right edges.
suggestion: Create a strict effects hierarchy: reserve the strongest glow for the hit line and active note, reduce background scanline/particle/grid opacity, and use one controlled chromatic offset on the title. Normalize pixel edge thickness, glow radius, and color roles for notes, lanes, score, button, and keycaps. Align each keycap precisely to its lane center with identical dimensions and spacing; add bottom/right safe-area to eliminate cropping. Raise contrast and reduce tracking on secondary copy, then ensure every panel edge and note is snapped to a consistent pixel grid.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
